questions.question: Which of the following implies convergence in distribution?

explanations.b: Convergence in probability implies convergence in distribution, but not the other way around. The hierarchy is:  $X_n \xrightarrow{a.s.} X \Rightarrow X_n \xrightarrow{p} X \Rightarrow X_n \xrightarrow{d} X$

questions.question: Which of the following best defines convergence in probability?

answers.d: The CDF of $X_n$ converges pointwise to the CDF of $X$

explanations.b: This is the formal definition of convergence in probability. It means that the probability of the random variable deviating from the limit by more than any $\epsilon$ vanishes.

questions.question: Which type of convergence is strongest among the following?

explanations.c: The strongest standard form is almost sure convergence. It implies convergence in probability, which in turn implies convergence in distribution.

questions.question: Let $F_{X_n}(x) = \begin{cases} 1 - \left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)^{nx}, & x > 0 \\ 0, & x \leq 0 \end{cases}$. What does $X_n$ converge to in distribution?

explanations.a: This is incorrect. The given CDF does not match the form of a Uniform distribution.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The limit does not yield the CDF of a Normal distribution.
explanations.c: Correct. As $n \to \infty$, $\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)^{nx} \to e^{-x}$, so $F_{X_n}(x) \to 1 - e^{-x}$, which is the CDF of an Exponential(1) distribution.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is not the form of a Poisson distribution CDF.

questions.question: What does convergence almost surely mean, informally?

answers.a: The probability that $X_n = X$ eventually is 1
answers.b: The average error $|X_n - X|$ goes to zero
answers.c: The values of $X_n$ get arbitrarily close to $X$ for almost all outcomes
answers.d: The distribution of $X_n$ matches that of $X$

explanations.c: The values of $X_n$ get arbitrarily close to $X$ for almost all outcomes. Almost sure convergence means that the sequence converges to $X$ for all $\omega \in \Omega$, except for a set of measure zero.
